config.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch

personas.name: Victor
personas.goals: Launch on November 12 no matter what
personas.hidden_agenda: Already told the board it's a done deal

personas.name: Hana
personas.goals: Don't launch a banking app that crashes
personas.hidden_agenda: Her team has been doing weekend shifts for a month

personas.name: Chloe
personas.goals: Ship something that works for everyone, including screen-reader users
personas.hidden_agenda: Lost the accessibility budget fight last quarter

personas.name: Ibrahim
personas.hidden_agenda: Was not invited to the board prep

pack.title: Aurora banking app - launch readiness review

agenda.title: Compliance sign-off
agenda.goal: Confirm what compliance still needs before launch

agenda.title: Rollout plan
agenda.goal: Agree the phases and the rollback trigger

agenda.title: The go/no-go call
agenda.goal: Make the call and agree what the board hears

facts.statement: Crash rate in the pilot = 0.6% of sessions
Load test peak = 8,000 requests per second

beats.summary: Victor cherry-picks; Hana corrects the crash rate; the CSAT inflation slips by
What's outstanding; Hana overstates the regulator notice; the accessibility number gets corrected late
Phases, load and the rollback trigger
The call; Victor's board promise comes out

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Bottom line, we're launching November twelfth, and this meeting is about how, not whether.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: With all due respect, that's exactly what this meeting is about.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Come on, Hana. The pilot went great. Crash rate's under a tenth of a percent.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: No. It's zero point six. Six times what you just said.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Zero point six, zero point one, it's a rounding error.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: It's not a rounding error on a banking app. People are moving money when it crashes.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: To be clear, most of the crashes are on the transfer screen. That's the scary one.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: And customers love it. Pilot CSAT was four point six.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Honestly, the comments are good. People like the new home screen.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: How many pilot customers was that?

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Fifteen hundred. Which is not a lot of phones.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Fifteen hundred real customers, real money. That's a real signal.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: How many blockers are still open? Because I have four.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Four, but two of them are basically done.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Basically done is not done.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: And accessibility. We're down to three open issues, which is huge progress.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: For the record, I'd want to see the accessibility list myself before launch.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Come on, three issues. We can patch those after.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: As far as I'm concerned, the transfer crash has to be fixed before launch.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Fine, fine. Who's on it?

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Marco's team. I'll get you a fix date from Marco by end of day tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: And somebody really needs to test the transfer flow with a screen reader.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Has the call center seen the new transfer flow? Because last time—

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Did anyone see the parking garage memo? They're moving us to level four.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Level four has no elevator access from the east side. It's a nightmare.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: I park on the street now. It's faster.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: The street? With my car? Absolutely not.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Strictly speaking, we were talking about the launch.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Fine. Compliance. Ibrahim, give me good news.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: There are two items outstanding. The disclosures text and the data retention review.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Two items. That's nothing.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: The retention review is not nothing. It's the one the regulator asked about last year.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: And don't we have to notify the regulator sixty days before launch?

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Thirty. It's a thirty-day notice.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Thirty days. When did we send it?

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: We haven't. Nobody told me there was a date until last week.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Come on, that's—

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: That's on us, not on him.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: For the record, if the notice goes out this week, the twelfth still works. Just.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: So it needs to go out this week.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: I'll file the regulator notice by Friday, if I get the final feature list from Chloe by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: To be clear, I can get you the feature list tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Then I'll file the notice on Thursday.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Bottom line, so compliance is a yes.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Strictly speaking, compliance is a "not yet".

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Sorry, I just pulled up the tracker. Accessibility is eleven open, not three. Three are the critical ones.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Eleven.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Three critical, that's what matters.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Honestly, eleven matters if you're the person who can't use the app.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Rollout. Hana, your plan?

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Phase one is five percent of customers. We watch it for a week before going wider.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: A week? Come on. Three days.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: A week. Banks don't get to move fast and break things.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Sorry, my laptop's about to die, let me grab a charger.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: What's the rollback trigger? Like, what number makes us pull it?

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Crash rate over one percent, or transfer failures over two percent, and we roll back. No meeting.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: No meeting is a bit much.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: No meeting is the point.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Has the load test been run at full scale?

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: It peaked at eight thousand requests a second without errors.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Eight thousand. See? It's ready.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: For phase one. Not for everyone at once.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Are we telling support what's in phase one? They had two hundred and thirty tickets from the pilot alone.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Support will be fine.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Support was not fine. Honestly, that's why the CSAT comments mention wait times.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Okay. Phase one at five percent, one week, with the rollback trigger as I said, automatic. That's the rollout. Decided.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Fine. A week.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: I'll brief the support leads on phase one before it starts.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Who's going to explain the rollback rule to the board, though?

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Honestly, I'm still thinking about the support queue.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Okay. The call. I want a go.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: With all due respect, it's a conditional go. Transfer crash fixed, regulator notice filed, critical accessibility issues closed.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: For the record, I agree with conditional.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Same.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Come on, the board demo is October thirtieth. I need to tell them something clean.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Tell them it's conditional. That is clean.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: I may have already told them it's a done deal.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: You what?

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Strictly speaking, you can't tell a board a launch is done before compliance signs off.

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Okay, okay. I hear you.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: So we're agreed? Conditional go for November twelfth, with the three conditions?

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Bottom line, yes. Conditional go for the twelfth, three conditions. Final.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Thank you. And the board?

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: I'll send the board an update on Monday with the conditions spelled out.

turns.speaker: Chloe
turns.text: Can I see that before it goes?

turns.speaker: Victor
turns.text: Fine. You can all see it.

turns.speaker: Ibrahim
turns.text: Thank you, Victor.
